Everything you need to publish the Lanternfly documentation, from install to the last component.

Lanternfly is an imaginary command-line tool that turns folders of notes into
searchable archives. It does not exist. It is here so this demo site has
something plausible to document, and so every component Pholio supports
appears on at least one page.
This is a demo site. Lanternfly is fictional; the components are real.

pushing the header down.

*Every page on this site went through exactly these four stages.*
Install Lanternfly with your package manager of choice and check that it runs.

Lanternfly runs on macOS, Linux and Windows. It needs about 20 MB of disk space
and nothing else.

The code tabs below share a group, so choosing a package manager here also
selects it on every other page that uses the same group.
Any shell works. On Windows, PowerShell is recommended.

You should see a single line such as `lanternfly 2.4.0`. Anything else means the
binary is not on your `PATH`.

Version 2 reads 1.x archives but writes a new format. Keep a copy of old
archives until every machine that opens them has been upgraded.
A file tree shows what `lanternfly init` creates. Folders can start open.

Never edit the `index` folder by hand. `lanternfly reindex` rebuilds it from
scratch.
Tabs with a default, grouped tabs that stay in sync, and single or multiple accordions.

`items` lists the labels, separated by `|`. Each `Tab` takes its `value` from
the matching label. With `updateAnchor`, choosing a tab also updates the URL
hash, so the link you copy opens that tab.
Pay each month, cancel any time.
Pay once a year and get two months free.

Tabs with the same `groupId` switch together. With `persist`, the choice is
remembered across pages and visits.

A label that itself contains a pipe is escaped: `items="a\|b|c"` yields the two
tabs "a|b" and "c".
Only one item is open at a time.
No. Archives are plain folders; use whatever sync tool you already trust.
Yes. `lanternfly export --all` writes one Markdown file per note.
Any number of items can be open.
`/` focuses search, `n` creates a note, `Esc` closes any dialog.

Markdown, plain text and PDF are indexed. Everything else is stored but not
searched.
Frontmatter, headings, links and images in the Markdown subset Pholio accepts.

A page is a Markdown file with frontmatter. The title comes from the
frontmatter, so the body starts at `##`.

Use `##` for sections and `###` for subsections. Headings become anchors and
entries in the table of contents on the right.

Ids are derived from the text, so this heading is reachable as
`#a-subsection`.

The options accepted by open(), as a type table.
Opens an archive. Every option is optional unless marked required.

<TypeTable
  type="{
  path: {
    description: 'Folder of the archive, absolute or relative to the working directory.',
    type: 'string',
    required: true,
  },
  watch: {
    description: 'Re-index files as they change on disk.',
    type: 'boolean',
    default: 'false',
  },
  limit: {
    description: 'Maximum number of hits a single search returns.',
    type: 'number',
    default: '50',
    typeDescription: 'Integer between 1 and 1000',
  },
  language: {
    description: 'Tokenizer used for new documents.',
    type: '"english" | "german"',
    default: '"english"',
  },
  legacyIndex: {
    description: 'Read the 1.x index format. Will be removed in version 3.',
    type: 'boolean',
    default: 'false',
    deprecated: true,
  },
}"
/>

<TypeTable
  type="{
  search: {
    description: 'Runs a query and resolves to the ranked hits.',
    type: '(query: string) => Promise<Hit[]>',
  },
  reindex: {
    description: 'Rebuilds the index from the files on disk.',
    type: '() => Promise<void>',
  },
  close: {
    description: 'Releases file handles. The archive cannot be used afterwards.',
    type: '() => void',
  },
}"
/>
